agenda_items.title: Knowledge Engineering as Ecosystem — Bridging Data Engineering, Information Architecture, and Knowledge Modeling
agenda_items.intent_description: Frame knowledge engineering as the creation of rich, multidisciplinary knowledge ecosystems — not IT development. The ecosystem bridges data engineering (facts and storage), information architecture (structure and navigation), and knowledge modeling (meaning and relationships). It is an end-to-end system handling capture, classification, and secure integration of internal and external knowledge across multiple workflows, products, and processes. Knowledge infrastructure is a business process in itself, not a single product.
requirements: Three domains: data engineering, information architecture, knowledge modeling
Crosses multiple workflows, products, and processes
Knowledge infrastructure = business process, not product

agenda_items.title: Knowledge Worker vs Knowledge Engineer — Technical Builders vs Ecosystem Participants
agenda_items.intent_description: Distinguish between knowledge engineers (technical experts who build the knowledge systems — design ontologies, implement pipelines, configure infrastructure) and knowledge workers (anyone contributing to or curating the knowledge ecosystem — domain experts entering information, reviewers validating outputs, consumers applying insights). Both roles are essential. The system must support both the technical builders who create the substrate and the domain participants who populate and validate it.
requirements: Knowledge engineers: build ontologies, pipelines, infrastructure
Knowledge workers: contribute, curate, validate, consume
System must support both roles with appropriate interfaces
